A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same independence-testing research, despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original test-power, type-I-error, ablation, variance, and training-time results on HDGM, Sinusoid, and RatInABox.

after.justification: Sections 6–7 and Appendix E report original experiments, including retained benchmarks, Wine Quality evaluation, NDS results, and new threshold and permutation diagnostics.

M1.justification: v1 optimizes HSIC power and separately trains InfoNCE/NWJ critics. v2 adds power-based NDS critic training, incorporating null and alternative moments and a threshold term in Equations (10) and (12). Algorithm 1 now covers both method families; the original HSIC objective and deep-kernel construction are retained.

E1.justification: v2 retains the three original datasets and adds Wine Quality, testing dependence between residual sugar and rated quality. Appendix E also evaluates an ISA bandwidth case and frequency-1 Sinusoid data. This extends coverage beyond the earlier synthetic and simulated benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: NDS is added to the comparisons against HSIC-D in Figures 1, 4, 5, 9, and 10. The existing named comparators, including MMD-D, C2ST-L/S, InfoNCE, NWJ, and the other HSIC variants, remain.

E3.justification: Original benchmark splits and training settings are largely retained. New protocols compare asymptotic, simulated-null, and permutation thresholds; vary MMD shuffle counts with 50 samples; and sweep ISA bandwidths and sample sizes. Wine adds 1,200 training samples and 10,000 training epochs.

E4.justification: The original HSIC-versus-SNR ablation and variance trajectories survive as Figures 11 and 13. v2 adds asymptotic-power checks, MMD shuffle-count analysis, ISA bandwidth sensitivity, threshold-term ablations, and statistic–threshold dependence diagnostics in Figures 2, 3, 6, 12, and 14–16.

E5.justification: Both versions report five training runs, standard-error bands for power-versus-test-size curves, standard-deviation bands for dataset-size curves, and 400 tests for type-I-error estimates. No revised seed, repetition, or uncertainty-reporting practice is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds NDS, Wine, and diagnostic results. Figure 16 reports power/correlation of 46%/37% for an NDS-trained critic versus 63%/98% for an InfoNCE-trained critic. The HDGM-20 dataset-size panel and training-time table are removed. The matched type-I-error table remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds NDS asymptotics and uniform-convergence proofs, shuffled-MMD concentration and variance propositions, and threshold-gradient derivations. The earlier HSIC convergence analysis largely moves from Appendix A to C. The new variance proof leading to Equation (22) fails to account for dependence in terms using the same permutation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the contribution from deep-HSIC kernel selection to representation learning for both MI/NDS and HSIC tests. MI-based testing already appeared in v1; NDS power optimization and claimed corrections to prior HSIC optimization work are new central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explains that optimizing NDS asymptotic power need not optimize permutation-test power, linking the discrepancy to statistic–threshold dependence. It also adds qualifications about comparing differently learned MMD/HSIC kernels and explains why threshold estimation can hurt HSIC training. These substantially extend v1's interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies NDS architecture sharing, Wine training details, explicit HSIC-Agg settings, and Gamma-threshold differentiation procedures. Most architecture tables, optimizer settings, batch size, and GPU information are retained. The earlier measured training times and their hardware context are removed.

R1.justification: v1 positions general kernel selection for independence testing as previously unaddressed. v2 explicitly engages with Ren et al. (2024), challenging its proof and threshold recommendations. It also expands references concerning MI estimation, HSIC asymptotics, threshold differentiation, and methods avoiding data splitting.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around an MI-first narrative. Sections are reordered, learning and theory are integrated, a discussion section is added, and retained appendix proofs are reorganized into assumptions, lemmas, propositions, and main results.

P2.justification: v2 adds multiple diagnostic plots and a statistic–threshold scatterplot, substitutes Wine panels into the main comparisons, moves the dimension comparison to Appendix E, and removes the timing table. Retained displays also receive revised legends, sizing, placement, and document typography.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially broadens empirical coverage and improves understanding of when asymptotic optimization fails to predict permutation-test power. However, its new MMD variance guarantee relies on Equation (22), whose expectation calculation incorrectly treats same-permutation terms as independent, leaving that guarantee unsupported. This material proof gap, alongside removed timing evidence, makes the net quality change uncertain despite the clear empirical and interpretive gains.
